production.note: US model years. Hagerty: "The 1990–93 models came with 200 hp". iSeeCars lists an 'AWD All-Trac Turbo 2dr Hatchback' for 1990 (iseecars-1990-celica), and KBB a '1993 Toyota Celica All-Trac Liftback 2D' (kbb-1993-celica-alltrac). No opened page states in so many words that 1993 was the last US model year.

body.note: Liftback only ('All-Trac Liftback 2D'); recorded as Coupe under the guide's rule for two-door sports cars with a rear liftback.

displacementL.note: 'a 200-horsepower, 2.0-liter turbocharged engine'. No opened page gave the cc figure.

aspiration.note: '2.0-liter turbocharged engine'; Hagerty: 'a water-air intercooler for the turbocharger'

transmission.note: The All-Trac 'came only with manual shift'; KBB lists 'Manual', '5 speed' (kbb-1992-celica-alltrac).

powerHp.note: PROVISIONAL (one named-author article, an unbylined article and a database; no Toyota or major-magazine source). Quote (Consumer Guide, Tom Appel): "The All-Trac (permanently engaged 4-wheel-drive) edition employed a 200-horsepower, 2.0-liter turbocharged engine and came only with manual shift." Hagerty (byline not confirmed): "The 1990–93 models came with 200 hp, interesting styling, and some driveline improvements over the first generation car." (hagerty-celica-alltrac). KBB 1992: "Horsepower: 200 @ 6000 RPM" (kbb-1992-celica-alltrac). No opened page reports a different US rating for 1990-1993.

weightLb.note: PROVISIONAL (database, single source for the launch year). 1990 All-Trac Turbo liftback, 5-speed manual (the only transmission). Quote (iSeeCars, 'AWD All-Trac Turbo 2dr Hatchback'): "Curb Weight | 3272 | lbs"; iSeeCars' 1991 page prints the same (iseecars-1991-celica). For 1992 iSeeCars gives 3,219 lb (iseecars-1992-celica) and KBB 3,218 lb ("Curb Weight: 3218 lbs.", kbb-1992-celica-alltrac); KBB 1993: 3,219 lb (kbb-1993-celica-alltrac). The 1992-1993 figures are 1.6% lower, which may be a model-year change; no page explains it.

sources.title: When a Rally-Bred Celica Was an Arcade Hero

provisionalNote: Power (200 hp) rests on one named-author article (Consumer Guide, Tom Appel), a Hagerty article whose byline could not be confirmed, and KBB, all agreeing, but no Toyota or major-magazine source. Weight (3,272 lb, 1990) rests on iSeeCars alone for 1990-1991 (a database); KBB and iSeeCars give 3,218-3,219 lb for 1992-1993. A Toyota US press kit or brochure, or a Car and Driver, Road & Track or MotorTrend specification panel, for the 1990 Celica All-Trac Turbo would replace both.
